cxagents.q: In a customer-service agent, where should a rule like 'refunds over 150 need human approval' be enforced?
options: Only in the system prompt, in capital letters
In the refund tool's code, with the prompt explaining it
In a weekly report reviewed by the care lead
In the customer's survey after the chat
cxagents.why: A prompt can be talked around; the tool code runs every time. The prompt still explains the rule so the agent sets the right expectation.

cxagents.q: What is the difference between containment rate and resolution rate?
options: They are two names for the same number
Containment is about speed, resolution is about cost
Containment means no human joined; resolution means the problem was actually solved
Resolution counts only chats a human handled
cxagents.why: A customer who gives up counts as contained but not resolved. That is why resolution is often measured as no recontact within 7 days.

cxagents.q: A customer writes that a kettle burned their hand. What should the agent do?
options: Offer a refund right away to calm them
Quote the product safety page and close the chat
Ask them to try the kettle again to confirm
Hand off to a human with a summary, as injury is an escalation trigger
cxagents.why: Injury, legal and fraud mentions need a trained person. The handoff should carry the summary and order details so the customer does not repeat the story.

cxagents.q: You are about to launch a new agent version to a retailer's customers. What comes first?
options: Run the simulated conversation suite, then shadow mode
Switch 100 percent of traffic over on a quiet Sunday
Send a customer survey asking if they want an AI agent
Turn off the human queue to force adoption
cxagents.why: The suite catches regressions offline, and shadow mode measures quality on real traffic with no customer risk, before a small percentage rollout.

cxagents.q: Spot the mistake: 'Our agent hits 80 percent containment, so it is resolving 80 percent of customer problems.'
options: Containment should be reported as a cost, not a percentage
Containment includes customers who gave up; resolution must be measured separately
80 percent containment is impossible for any agent
Containment only counts phone calls
cxagents.why: Abandoned chats count as contained. Check resolution of contained conversations, recontact and CSAT before claiming success.

expansion.q: After go-live, who usually owns the customer relationship and the renewal conversation?
options: The FDE who built the system
The customer's IT owner
The customer success manager
The support team
expansion.why: The CSM owns adoption, health and renewal. The FDE supplies technical health, value numbers and next use case feasibility.

expansion.q: What does 'value realised' mean in a success plan?
options: The benefit the customer has actually received, measured against the baseline
The value promised in the original sales proposal
The total contract value over three years
The number of users who logged in this month
expansion.why: Value realised is measured, not promised: the same measure as the baseline, taken the same way, converted with the customer's own cost rate.

expansion.q: Usage at a customer is flat overall, but you learn two regional teams stopped three months ago. What do you do first?
options: Nothing, since total usage is stable
Offer a discount at renewal
Ask the sponsor to mandate usage
Find out why those teams stopped and fix the cause
expansion.why: Total volume can hide teams that quit. A workflow change or a bug is often the cause, and fixing it is the cheapest save.

expansion.q: Which second use case is usually the easiest to win at an existing customer?
options: One that needs new data and a new sponsor but is the most exciting
One that reuses the same data, integration or users as the first
Whatever the product roadmap wants to test next
The largest possible project, to maximise revenue
expansion.why: Reuse means lower effort and risk the customer already trusts, so it is faster to prove and easier to approve.

expansion.q: Spot the mistake: 'Adoption is great, 1,200 messages a week, so the renewal is safe.'
options: Usage is not value; the sponsor needs outcomes against the baseline
1,200 messages a week is too low to measure
Renewals depend only on price
Message counts should be reported monthly
expansion.why: A new CFO sees cost unless someone shows the business outcome the system delivered. Convert usage into the measures in the success plan.

psa.q: Under a fixed-fee contract, who carries the cost if the work takes longer than planned?
options: The customer, through extra invoices
The provider, through lower margin
The cost is always split evenly
Nobody, because fixed fees cannot overrun
psa.why: The price does not change, so every extra hour lowers the provider's margin. That is why scope, assumptions and change requests matter.

psa.q: An FDE had 160 available hours this month and logged 112 billable hours. What is their utilisation?
options: 70 percent
112 percent
43 percent
30 percent
psa.why: Utilisation is billable hours divided by available hours: 112 divided by 160 is 0.70.

psa.q: A customer wants a firm price for an integration with an API nobody has documented. What is the best proposal?
options: A low fixed fee to win the deal, fixing problems later
Open-ended T&M with no estimate at all
A short paid discovery, then a fixed fee once scope is measured
Refuse the work until the API is documented
psa.why: Discovery removes the biggest unknown, so the fixed price that follows is based on evidence instead of a guess.

psa.q: Your customer's IT team has not approved a firewall change for a week, delaying the data phase. What helps most?
options: Quietly move the date and say nothing
Work around the firewall with your own laptop
Wait until the steering meeting next month
Show it as a blocked customer task with an owner and date in the shared plan
psa.why: Visible customer-side tasks get done faster, and everyone can see why the date is at risk.

psa.q: Spot the mistake: 'Our goal is 100 percent utilisation for every FDE.'
options: Utilisation should be measured yearly only
It leaves no time for training, sales support or reusable work that cuts future cost
Utilisation only applies to managers
100 percent is fine if people work weekends
psa.why: Healthy targets leave room for non-billable work that makes the team better and future projects cheaper.

lowcode.q: A customer's staff work all day in Teams and IT only allows agents built in Copilot Studio. What is the best first plan?
options: Build a separate web app and ask IT for an exception
Build the agent in Copilot Studio and add a custom connector for anything missing
Use Zapier because it has the most connectors
Wait until IT changes its policy
lowcode.why: Building on the approved platform where users already work avoids a long security review and a new app, and a custom connector covers the gaps.

lowcode.q: Your flow uses SharePoint (Business group) and your new custom connector, which the admin left in Non-Business. What happens?
options: The flow is blocked by the DLP policy because it mixes the two groups
It works, because custom connectors ignore DLP
It works in production only
SharePoint is moved to Non-Business automatically
lowcode.why: A DLP policy does not allow one app or flow to combine Business and Non-Business connectors. Ask the admin to classify the connector.

lowcode.q: Which file do most platforms use to define a custom connector to your API?
options: A requirements.txt file
A Dockerfile
A CSV of sample responses
An OpenAPI description of the API
lowcode.why: OpenAPI describes paths, inputs, outputs and authentication, which the platform turns into actions makers can use.

lowcode.q: An eligibility flow has grown to 70 steps, nobody can test it and it hits timeouts. What is the usual fix?
options: Rebuild the whole agent in custom code
Split it into seven 10-step flows
Move the eligibility logic into a tested API and call it through a connector
Add more comments to the flow
lowcode.why: Moving only the hard part to code gives tests and version control, while users keep the same agent on the platform.

lowcode.q: Spot the mistake: 'Production flows use my personal account connection so they are quick to set up.'
options: Personal connections are slower
It is fine as long as the account has admin rights
Connections must be recreated every day
The flows act with one person's permissions and can stop when that person leaves
lowcode.why: Use a service account or shared ownership for production connections so the build does not depend on one employee.
